overview.title: Speak Chat
overview.subtitle: Read chat messages aloud on your stream

blocks.x: Speak Chat turns chat messages into speech and plays them on your stream through an OBS overlay. You decide what triggers them: a command, bits, a channel points reward, a role or every message.
It works with a standard voice included in your plan and optional premium voices. The audio is generated on the server, so it sounds the same in any OBS.

items: A viewer triggers the reading according to the rules you set.
The server applies the filters (cooldowns, length and blocks) and generates the audio.
The OBS overlay plays the audio and shows, if you want, a balloon with the user and their message.
What triggers the reading and which roles can use it.
The voice, language, quality and volume.
Cooldowns, maximum length, blocked words and users.
The look and position of the balloon on screen.

blocks.x: If you have an account, the step-by-step setup is in the dashboard help center:

setup.title: Speak Chat: getting started
setup.subtitle: Turn it on, put the overlay in OBS and run a test

blocks.x: Open Funciones → Speak Chat (`/features/speak-chat`). In the General tab turn on “Speak Chat active”. It starts off: while it is off, nothing is read even if the rules are fine. To configure and test it you need the Moderation level or higher in the dashboard.

The page has 13 tabs (details below). The first one, Guide, walks you through four steps. Everything is saved with the “Save” button, which only turns on when there are changes; if you try to leave with unsaved changes, the panel warns you.

head: Tab
What it is for
rows: Four steps to get it working (turn it on, pick the voice, put the link in OBS and send a test). Each step shows whether it is done and takes you to its tab.
The “Speak Chat active” switch and a warning if no overlay is connected in OBS.
The five rules that make a message get read (command, bits, channel points, role and all messages) and who can use each one.
Commands like `!goku` with their own voice, permissions and cooldowns.
The voice Speak Chat reads with when a command has none of its own: voice type, quality, language, voice and volume.
Every voice you can use; you listen to the character ones and set one as the channel voice with a click.
Search for a character voice, listen to its sample and request it so Decatron can approve it.
Your own list of character voices (Patrocinador rank or higher).
Cooldowns, maximum length, blocked words and blocked users.
Look and position of the balloon, the OBS links (All, Twitch only, Kick only) with their status, and reload overlays.
Your voice balance: monthly quota, purchased credits and standard characters, with a low-balance warning.
Who changed the settings, when and which fields.
Send a test message to the overlay.

blocks.x: On the right of the panel (below it on mobile) there is a fixed column with the balloon preview, the Speak Chat and OBS status, your voice balance and a “Send test” button.
All rules start off. Turn on at least one in the Activación tab; for example, the `!tts` command.

The Guide and the Overlay tab show the overlay link, in the format `/overlay/speak-chat?channel=your_channel`. Add it as a “Browser” source in OBS, with your scene's width and height, and clear the custom CSS OBS adds by default so the background is transparent. With both channels linked you will see three links (“All”, “Twitch only” and “Kick only”); each one shows whether it is connected in OBS. Audios play one at a time, in order of arrival.
If you change the configuration, overlays update on their own; the reload button does it instantly.

In the Tests tab you type a message and send it to the overlay (there is also a “Send test” button in the right-hand column). If Speak Chat is off or no overlay is connected, the panel warns you; the server also rejects the test with “Speak Chat está desactivado”. The test uses the voice you see on screen even if you have not saved it, and it generates real audio, so it uses the same balance as a real message.
If the audio is generated but does not play, the most common cause is that the overlay is not connected in OBS. Check that the source is in the scene and visible.
The History tab shows every time someone saved the settings: who it was, when, and which fields changed, with the value before and after. The last 100 saves are kept.

If something plays when it should not, or stops playing, this shows whether someone changed a rule or turned the main switch off. Each field appears with its name and values in plain language (for example “Rule 6 · permission: everyone”); hovering over it shows its technical path, such as `global.enabled`.

activation.title: Speak Chat: activation rules
activation.subtitle: What makes a message be read and who can trigger it

blocks.x: There are five rules, each with its own switch. All start off. A message is read if it meets any of the turned-on rules.

head: Rule
What it does
Default
rows: The viewer types the command followed by the text, for example `!tts Hello streamer`, and “Hello streamer” is read. The command must be complete: `!tts` is not triggered by `!ttsx`.
When someone sends that many bits or more with a message, the message is read.
When a specific reward is redeemed, which you choose from the list of your rewards or by pasting its ID, the redemption text is read. A redemption without text is ignored.
Any message from those with an enabled role is read.
Absolutely the whole chat is read.

blocks.x: “Todos los mensajes” and “Por rol” read messages without anyone asking and use credits or quota on each one. Use them together with the cooldown and maximum length filters.

Besides the main command in the Activation tab you can add as many as you like in the Voice commands tab with “Add voice command”. Each one has its own name (`!goku`, `!narrator`…), its own voice and its own permissions: `!tts` keeps the channel's voice while `!goku` speaks with Goku's.

items: Own voice: standard (free), premium or character. The last two need voice credits; a Free account can use them if it bought credits.

If there is no balance (paid voices only): by default the voice does not play and the bot warns in chat, at most once every 5 minutes per command. You can choose to read it with the standard voice instead.
Own cooldowns: each command can have its own; if left empty it inherits the channel's (Filters tab).

Limit per rank: how many commands with their own voice you can have depends on your rank (Free 3, Supporter 10, Premium 30, Patrocinador 100, Fundador no practical limit). Dropping rank deletes nothing: you just cannot add more.
Everything is charged to the channel's credits, like the main voice. Two commands with the same name: only the first one in the list works.

blocks.x: Speak Chat also reads Kick chat. The platform is chosen with the OBS link, like On-screen chat: «All» reads Twitch and Kick together, «Twitch only» and «Kick only» separate scenes. A command typed on a platform that no connected overlay reads is neither generated nor charged. Bits and channel points are Twitch-only. Your previous links keep reading Twitch only until you use the «All» link.

items: With both channels linked, the Overlay tab shows the «All» link (recommended): a single OBS overlay that plays Twitch and Kick with one voice queue. Below, under Advanced, the «Twitch only» and «Kick only» links.
Each link shows whether it is connected in OBS right now. If the «All» link and a single-platform link are connected at once, the panel warns that every message would play twice.
Settings and credits are those of your account (the main channel), also when you sign in with Kick. Old links keep working.

blocks.x: The command, bits, channel points and role rules have a list of roles: Todos, Subs, VIPs, Mods and Streamer. If “Todos” is checked, the rest is not looked at. Lead moderators count as moderators.

When a redemption arrives as a channel points event, Twitch does not report the redeemer's badges: it only tells whether they are the streamer. For rewards, leave the rule on “Todos” so anyone can redeem it.
The same redemption can arrive twice (as a chat message and as a points event). Only the first is read: repeats from the same user and reward are discarded for 30 seconds.

voice.title: Speak Chat: voice and credits
voice.subtitle: Engine, language, voice, volume and what is charged

head: Engine
How it sounds
Cost
rows: Runs on our server. It is the default engine.
Comes from your plan's standard voice quota, in characters, without using credits.
More voices and languages, including Japanese. There are two qualities: Normal and Alta calidad.
Credits per character; Alta calidad costs more than Normal.
Character voices chosen by the Decatron team. They appear in the engine's "Character voice" drop-down.
Credits per byte of text (an accented vowel or "ñ" weighs 2 bytes). The current rate is on `/credits`.

blocks.x: Character voices come from a catalog approved by Decatron, with each voice's language and author. If a voice stops being available, the catalog's default voice is used. If you run out of credits or the synthesis fails, the chat is not left silent: it is read with the standard voice.

Can't find the voice you want? In the Request voice tab, search for the character, listen to each result's sample and press “Request this voice” on the one you like (searching and listening cost no credits). If you can't find it, describe it in your own words under “Can't find it?”. You can have up to 3 requests under review at once and see the status of each one (under review, approved, or rejected with the reason). If it is approved, the voice appears in the list for everyone. With the Patrocinador rank (or higher) the My voices tab lets you search Fish, listen to the sample and add up to 10 voices to your list without waiting for approval; they show in your list with the “mine” mark, only in your channel and while you keep the rank. The licence of each voice is its author's. The Voice library tab lists every available voice (character ones with their sample) and “Use in channel” sets one as the channel voice.
Each plan's standard quota and the current premium voice rates are on the credits page (`/credits`). Premium voices are only available if your account has credits or is unlimited.

items: Voice engine, and in Premium the quality.
Language: the available voices depend on the language and come from the server catalog.
Voice: a specific one, or “Automática” (the first of the language). Each engine remembers its own choice, so switching engines does not lose the other.
Audio volume, from 0 to 100 (80 by default).

blocks.x: With a premium voice, if you run out of credits chat does not go silent: it is read with the standard voice until your monthly quota runs out. If the language does not exist in the standard voice (Japanese), it will sound in Spanish.

The Credits tab shows your voice balance: the monthly quota (it resets on the 1st), purchased credits (they do not expire) and the standard voice characters you have left, with a warning when it runs low and another when it runs out; the balance is also in the fixed right-hand column. Buy credits from the credits page.

If in the last 7 days any reading fell back to the standard voice because the chosen voice could not be generated (no credits, voice unavailable or engine failure), the Credits tab says so, with the count and the most frequent reason.
In each channel only one voice plays at a time among Speak Chat, event alerts, tips and timers. Those that arrive while another is speaking wait for their turn, in order of arrival.

items: Up to 10 voices can wait per channel; if the queue fills up, the oldest is discarded.
A voice that waits more than 30 seconds is discarded: the alert still appears, without voice, and nothing is charged.
If Speak Chat and event alerts are about to read the same text within 30 seconds (for example, a bits message), it is read only once.

blocks.x: The turn is released when the overlay reports it finished speaking. If two Speak Chat overlays are open at once, the audio will sound duplicated: keep only one.

filters.title: Speak Chat: filters, balloon and tests
filters.subtitle: Limit what is read and customize what is seen

head: Setting
What it does
Default
rows: Minimum seconds between any read message. 0 turns it off.
Minimum seconds between messages from the same user.
A longer message is cut to that length (it is not discarded).

blocks.x: Before reading a message, Speak Chat can remove what should not be spoken. It is set in the Filters tab and applied before the maximum length and before charging: whatever is removed is neither read nor paid for.

items: Links: remove them, replace them with “link” or leave them. Addresses with `http(s)://`, with `www.` and bare domains with a known ending (`.com`, `.tv`, `.gg`…) count; “ok.thanks” is not a link.

Emotes: Twitch and Kick emotes, 7TV, BTTV and FFZ emotes and the channel’s own are skipped. Third-party emotes are looked up with a wait limit: if the catalog is slow, that message is read without skipping them.
Repeated letters: “heyyyyyy” is read “heyy” and “!!!!!” is read “!”.
Emojis and symbols: removed so each one’s name is not read.

blocks.x: Channels that already had Speak Chat saved stay as they were until they turn cleanup on; new channels start with links and emotes removed and repeated letters shortened (emojis are left). If nothing is left after cleanup, the message is dropped. Kick messages are never read as “[emote:123:NAME]” again.

items: Blocked words (one per line): a message containing any of them is not read, regardless of case. Below you choose how they are matched: whole word (recommended, "ass" does not block "class") or any fragment. Your previous setup stays on fragment until you change it.
Blocked users (one per line): their messages are not read.

blocks.x: In the Overlay tab you turn the balloon with the user and their message on or off. You can choose the position (top or bottom, left, center or right; bottom left by default), the background and text colors, the font size (16 px by default) and how long it shows (5,000 ms by default). The balloon stays that long after the audio ends, and messages are shown one at a time. There is a preview in the same tab.

The Tests tab sends a test message to the overlay (by default “Hello, this is a Speak Chat test message”). It goes through the same cleanup as a real message. While you type it shows what would be read and what it would cost (credits with premium or character voices; with the standard voice, the characters from your quota), without generating audio or spending anything. It requires Speak Chat to be on, and the test itself does use your balance like a real message.
